newsitem.title: USA: Fine Air shares seen pressured after crash.
newsitem.headline: Fine Air shares seen pressured after crash.

text.p: With less than two days' trade under its wings, Fine Air Services Inc shares could come under further pressure as investors evaluate the financial impact of a crash on Thursday of one of its cargo jets, analysts said.

Trading in the stock, which went public on Wednesday, was halted on Nasdaq on news a Fine Air DC-8, made by Boeing Co's McDonnell Douglas Corp, crashed near Miami International Airport. At least three people were killed.
The stock was off 1-1/4 to 14-5/8 when it was halted. A Nasdasq spokesman said it was unclear when trade would resume.
David Menlow, president of IPO Financial Network Corp, based in Spingfield, N.J., said he thought that much would depend on Fine Air's legal liability in the crash.
"I think the shares will be hostage to a vein of fear in the absence of hard facts," he said.
Fine Air's stock priced at $14.50 per share on Wednesday and hit a high of 17-1/8 in its first day of trading.

"It's up in the air right now what financial impact this will have on the company, but I'm confident that over time the company will be able to muddle through," said Manish Shah, editor and publisher for IPO Maven.
A spokesman for Fine Air said the company was preparing a statement on the crash to be released later Thursday.
Shah followed Fine Air's progress leading up to its market debut. "The next two quarters will be critical," he added.
According to its IPO filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Fine Air had a fleet of 15 DC-8's and also relies on interline relationships with more than 50 airlines.
Fine Air sold 8.5 million shares to become a public company in a deal that generated $123.3 million.

Shah said the timing of the crash was doubly unfortunate. Not only did it draw negative publicity to Fine Air at a time when the company is on investors' radar screens, but the crash also came at a time when the IPO was enjoying business spillover from a strike by United Parcel Service of America Inc workers.
Fine Air is the largest international air cargo carrier serving Miami International Airport and a leading provider of services between the United States and Latin America.
